questions.question: A balance shows 6 + 4 on the left and 5 + 5 on the right. Is it even?
questions.explain: Add each side: 6+4 is 10 and 5+5 is 10, so the balance is even. Different numbers can still make the same total.

questions.question: A balance shows 9 + 1 on the left and 7 + 3 on the right. Is it even?
questions.explain: 9+1 is 10 and 7+3 is 10, so both sides are the same. You do not need the same numbers, just the same total.

questions.question: A balance shows 7 + 5 on the left and 8 + 3 on the right. Is it even?
questions.explain: 7+5 is 12 and 8+3 is 11, so the balance tips. Check the totals, not just whether the numbers look the same.

questions.question: A balance shows 4 + 8 on the left and 6 + 6 on the right. Is it even?
questions.explain: 4+8 is 12 and 6+6 is 12, so it is even. Two different pairs of numbers can make the same total.

questions.question: Sam has 5 red marbles and 4 blue ones. Lea has 6 red and 3 blue. Do they have the same total?
questions.explain: Sam has 5+4, which is 9. Lea has 6+3, which is also 9. Different colours can still give the same total.

questions.question: Mia puts 8 crackers and 2 cubes on a plate. Ben puts 5 crackers and 5 cubes. Are the totals the same?
questions.explain: 8+2 is 10 and 5+5 is 10, so both plates have 10 treats. The mix can be different but the total is the same.

questions.question: Ava has 9 stickers and 4 more. Kai has 7 stickers and 5 more. Do they have the same total?
questions.explain: Ava has 9+4, which is 13. Kai has 7+5, which is 12. Since 13 is not 12, the totals are different.

questions.question: Lily bakes 6 cookies and 4 muffins. Tom bakes 8 cookies and 2 muffins. Are the totals the same?
questions.explain: 6+4 is 10 and 8+2 is 10, so both bakers made 10 treats. Different recipes can give the same total.

questions.question: Zoe says 7 + 6 = 8 + 5 is NOT true because the numbers are different. Is Zoe right or wrong?
questions.explain: 7+6 is 13 and 8+5 is 13, so the sentence IS true. You check the totals, not whether the numbers look the same.

questions.question: Maya says 12 + 5 = 14 + 4 is true because both sides have big numbers. Is Maya right?
questions.explain: 12+5 is 17 and 14+4 is 18, so the sentence is false. Big numbers do not mean the totals match.

questions.question: Sam says 4 + 9 = 6 + 7 is NOT true because the numbers are different. What is Sam doing wrong?
options: He only checks the left side
questions.explain: 4+9 is 13 and 6+7 is 13, so the sentence IS true. Sam thinks the numbers must be the same, but only the totals need to match.

questions.question: Ines wrote 3 + 8 = 5 + 6 and said it is NOT true because 3 is not 5. Is Ines right or wrong?
questions.explain: 3+8 is 11 and 5+6 is 11, so the sentence IS true. Ines compared single numbers instead of adding both sides.
